pull_request.body:
The TL;DR had become a definition chain: agentic system, machinery, factory,
factory learns, all before anything contestable. It summarized the article's
setup rather than its bet, and nothing in it could turn out to be false.

Restore the shape the TL;DR had before 30f569e and 9fca4f9 removed it — a
stake, a concession, and a testable bet — without restoring the overclaim
those commits were right to cut. Recursive construction and closure stay
framed as what makes the question worth asking, not as results the program
has established, so the summary no longer contradicts the stronger-claims
table. Names theory-mediated learning with a short gloss, since the title
moved away from that term and a public reader arrives without it.

Drops the recursive-self-improvement label; the closure it described and the
contrast with training new models stay in plain wording.

commits.messageBody:
The summary claimed improvement without training new models but never said
why that is available, leaving the reader to supply the mechanism. Addressable
storage is the reason: a retained change is a write, so neither catastrophic
forgetting nor loss of plasticity applies.

Scopes the claim to retention rather than to continual learning as a whole.
The unrestricted form would contradict sutton-javed-why-ai-models-stop-learning,
retained in kb/sources/ as a counterpoint arguing that context-state adaptation
cannot replace continual weight learning, and the body carries no rebuttal to
it. The scoped form also sets up the bet instead of sitting beside it: cheap
retention relocates the difficulty to selection and coherence, which is what
theory-mediated learning is proposed to address.

The body's continual-learning section does not yet develop this framing; it
argues the retention path without naming the storage substrate.
commits.messageHeadline: Name addressable storage as what makes retention cheap in the TLDR

commits.messageBody:
The previous TLDR claimed cheap retention makes continual learning easy. That
attacks a position Sutton and Javed do not hold: the retained interview has
them conceding context-state adaptation outright, and resting the weight
requirement on concept and abstraction formation instead. It also collides
with continual-learning-requires-governing-behaviour-changing-writes, which
argues continual learning needs governed writes beyond stored content.

Aims the disagreement where the ingest's own limitations locate it: the
interview does not establish continued weight change as the necessary
component boundary, and never compares its update space with evidence-
responsive artifact learning. Sutton names self-consistency under continued
self-training as his lab's biggest ambition, so both programs agree coherence
is the hard problem and differ on substrate. The claim is now that coherence
is more tractable where the learned material can be read, which is falsifiable
against the strategy-change conditions the article already lists.

The body still cites none of the coevolution note cluster this claim rests on.
commits.messageHeadline: Contest weight-necessity on coherence rather than on retention

commits.messageBody:
The article argued its position against Sutton's later bet until f44b73e, which
cut the section while removing the Naur material; Sutton mentions went from five
to one to none. The TLDR meanwhile grew a claim about coherence and readable
learning that the body neither stated nor sourced.

Restores the section under the factory framing, keeping the earlier reading of
the retained quote: Sutton and Javed allow context in the agent's state and
require weight change on top of it, so the disagreement is over the necessity
of weight updates for concept formation, not over whether anything can be
learned outside weights. Overstating it as exclusivity would misread a quote
that says it could be both.

Adds the coherence argument the TLDR now leads with. Sutton names self-
consistency under continued self-training as his lab's largest goal, so both
programs treat coherence as the hard part and differ on substrate; the bet is
that readable retained material makes inspection, testing, and withdrawal
possible where weights do not. Cites the coevolution note cluster the claim
rests on.

Workshop: kb/work/theory-mediated-self-improvement-series
commits.messageHeadline: Restore the Sutton disagreement and ground the coherence claim
